verdicts.reason: A is broken on several counts. The headline is centred on an off-centre axis, which leaves the left third dead, and it wraps to leave 'sunshine.' alone on its own line. The italic subline is nearly as large as the headline, which flattens the hierarchy. The CTA is left-aligned at a different x than the centred text above it and sits cramped near the bottom edge. B keeps the original centred stack, line break and order intact, but it is just a shrunk copy of the original rather than a rearranged one. Its 'Now in four flavours' subline is so tiny it is effectively unreadable, the CTA is undersized, and the wide sides are left empty, so it is not built for a banner. Even so, it is coherent and well aligned, which makes it the less bad of the two.
